articles.title: AMAZON IS REDESIGNING PRIME VIDEO WITH MORE AI, BUT WILL IT FIX WHAT FRUSTRATES VIEWERS?
articles.summary: Amazon is overhauling Prime Video's home screen through an internal project called Lighthouse, personally driven by Jeff Bezos, replacing the static tile grid with AI-generated, personalized recommendations. The redesign follows a tense meeting last fall where Bezos pushed executives to lean harder into AI. It remains unclear whether AI-driven rankings will genuinely reduce paid placement bias or simply shift it into the algorithm, leaving real benefits to viewers uncertain until testing expands beyond the current small user group.

articles.title: HYUNDAI MOTOR GROUP OPENS UX RESEARCH HUB IN SHANGHAI
articles.summary: Hyundai Motor Group has opened UX Studio Shanghai, a dedicated user experience research hub in Jing'an district, completing its four-city network alongside Seoul, Frankfurt, and Irvine facilities. The three-story studio splits into a public Open Lab, with Explorer, Test, and Archive zones, and an invite-only Advanced Lab housing a simulation platform for concept-to-validation co-development.

articles.title: WHATSAPP TESTING NEW MESSAGE BUBBLES ON IOS
articles.summary: WhatsApp is testing redesigned chat bubbles on iOS that feature significantly rounder, softer corners, bringing them closer to iMessage and better aligning with its recent Liquid Glass redesign. The update also removes the green outlines around photos, videos, GIFs, and link previews for a cleaner, more integrated appearance. The changes are currently limited to select TestFlight users, with no confirmed date for a wider rollout.

articles.title: IOS 27'S NEW SIRI DELIVERS IN EVERY SINGLE WAY I'D HOPED FOR
articles.summary: iOS 27 introduces a major AI-powered Siri upgrade that addresses three key weaknesses: world knowledge, conversational interactions, and consistency across Apple devices. Siri can now answer broad questions, maintain conversations with follow-ups and chat history, and provide the same capabilities across iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch, iPad, and, eventually, Apple TV and HomePod. Deep integration with Apple apps also enables personalized assistance based on messages, notes, and email, potentially giving Siri a significant advantage for everyday Apple users.

articles.title: A SIDE PROJECT IS THE FASTEST WAY TO UPSKILL IN THE AGE OF AI
articles.summary: Building small side projects is one of the fastest ways for UX professionals to learn how AI is changing software development, with tools like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor dramatically lowering the technical, time, and cost barriers to creating real products. Rather than relying on highly abstracted tools like Lovable, working closer to the actual development process—doing discovery and design, learning concepts such as version control, and asking AI to explain unfamiliar technology—builds much deeper practical knowledge. The key is to build with AI rather than have AI build everything for you, gaining technical fluency and end-to-end product-building skills through hands-on experience.

articles.title: WORKING BACKWARDS
articles.summary: A visit to an art school studio shows how painting habits mirror the judgment senior designers build over time. Design differs from art in serving someone else's outcome, yet deliberate practice—training the eye as art students do—builds taste no tool can replace. As prompts turn ideas into finished apps within days, skipping the slow, layer-by-layer deconstruction that art students practice may cost designers the deeper judgment such practice builds.

articles.title: MAKE VIDEO USABLE AS DATA AND MEMORY FOR AI
articles.summary: VideoDB turns files, live streams, and camera feeds into persistent, searchable context that AI applications and agents can retrieve and act on.

articles.title: ANATOMY'S CAMPAIGN FOR THE HORNIMAN MUSEUM IS BUILT ON A BESPOKE TYPEFACE FORAGED FROM ITS COLLECTIONS AND GARDENS
LEARNING BEFORE LEVERAGE
articles.summary: A design team's rollout of Claude Code in February revealed pressure to appear competent before actually mastering the tool, echoing a similar pattern at Slack. Drawing on researchers and practitioners, the piece argues AI adoption should be treated as reversible experimentation built on candor, shared vocabulary, and coordinated workflow changes across design and engineering. Survey data showing most designers feel overwhelmed and pressured to do more underscores the case for making uncertainty visible rather than hidden.

articles.title: WHY I DON'T USE INTERRUPTION PAGES
articles.summary: A UX reviewer argues against using interruption pages, a GOV.UK Design System pattern meant to pause users with warnings mid-journey. Interruption pages offer multiple actions, use unconventional button labels, and look like dismissible banners rather than part of the form flow. A standard question with radio buttons is recommended instead, since it forces conscious decisions without needing a visually distinct screen.

articles.title: THE “PIXEL POLICE” ARE RETIRED: WHY AI AGENTS ARE THE NEW MEDIATORS OF WEB DESIGN
articles.summary: AI agents are eliminating the traditional designer-developer handoff, letting teams build live together in real time instead of manually translating Figma files into code.

articles.title: EVERYONE'S SAYING THE SAME THING ABOUT THE NEW COCA-COLA FONT
articles.summary: Coca-Cola's newly overhauled brand identity, designed by JKR, gives greater prominence to the "Better With" serif typeface, created by Brody Associates in 2023 for a holiday campaign.
